appraisal_events.evidence: « Dire que pour une fois il n'avait pas menti, c'est incroyable », eût pensé Bloch.
appraisal_events.explanation: In an ironic aside hypothetically attributed to him, Bloch treats M. de Marsantes's rare truthful praise as remarkable, implying he is habitually dishonest.

appraisal_events.evidence: Charlus ... quitta brusquement M. de Faffenheim avec qui il causait, fit un tour rapide qui l'amena en face de moi; « faites-moi donc le plaisir de venir me voir »; « j'aimerais mieux vous expliquer cela plus tranquillement »
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus abruptly abandons his conversation to seek out the narrator and presses a private, insistent invitation, singling him out for special attention, though his guarded, calculating manner leaves the value of this favor uncertain.

status_effects.explanation: Bloch's ironic aside casts mild doubt on M. de Marsantes's habitual truthfulness, though the reference is layered through hypothetical narration.
The narrator is singled out for a private audience by the socially eminent Charlus, a mark of inclusion, though delivered with an unsettling, controlling tone.

ambiguities: The referent of 'il' in Bloch's imagined remark ('il n'avait pas menti') most plausibly points to M. de Marsantes (implying habitual dishonesty), but the hypothetical construction 'eût pensé' makes it unclear whether this is a genuine attributed thought or purely the narrator's ironic invention.

Charlus's motive in singling out the narrator is ambiguous — it could read as social favor/elevation or as a subtly controlling, calculating overture; the narrator's own unease ('avec inquiétude') leaves the valence unresolved.
